name: Ironwail
summary: A high-performance QuakeSpasm fork for modern GPUs. Windows and Linux; not macOS.
description:
Ironwail is a QuakeSpasm derivative built for large modern maps, and it needs a modern OpenGL core context to do it. That is the reason for the macOS entry below: upstream publishes no macOS build, and macOS does not provide the OpenGL version Ironwail asks for, so the honest answer is `unsupported` and not `unverified`.

This profile was written from Ironwail's own published command-line documentation, not from a build running on this machine. That is what every `unverified` platform below means, and it is why there is no version probe: asking a Quake engine what version it is means starting it, and starting it means opening a window and a game.

`play_map` names a game directory as well as a map, because that is what these engines' command lines do: `-game` chooses which directory the map is loaded from. Launching a map into a directory nobody named is how you end up watching the wrong map.

license.notice: Quake engine source ports are separate programs under their own licences. This profile configures one; it does not contain, link or relicense it. Game data — PAK files, maps, textures and sounds shipped with a commercial release — is not covered by that licence, and the Companion never copies, uploads or redistributes it.

platforms.note: Upstream publishes Windows builds; nobody here has run one. The command line is Ironwail's own documented one.
Ironwail builds from source on Linux and upstream publishes no Linux binary; nobody here has run one.
